classification.difficultyReason: Use the supplied right triangle to select tangent from the horizontal distance and required height, then multiply 12 by tan 37 degrees.

content.prompt: When felling a tree that is close to a house, it’s wise to first determine its height. At a point 12 metres from the base of a tree, the angle of elevation to the topmost point on the tree is $37^{\circ}$. How tall is the tree? Give your answer to two decimal places.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 4, left column, diagram beneath the stem
spec.description: An unfilled right triangle with a horizontal 12 m base, a 37-degree elevation angle at the left endpoint, and a vertical tree-height segment on the right. The sight line joins the observation point to the tree top. The decorative tree is replaced by the vertical height line.
spec.mathematics: The unknown vertical height is opposite 37 degrees and the horizontal distance of 12 m is adjacent. The base and height are perpendicular.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; no calculated height is supplied.

answer.worked:
Let $h$ metres be the height of the tree.
$$\begin{align*}\tan 37^{\circ} &= \frac{h}{12}\\h &= 12\tan 37^{\circ}\\h &\approx 9.04\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
